title: Optogenetic manipulation of cellular communication in axolotls
protocol: Thaw the required plasmids for this experiment.
Dilute DNA constructs in DPBS to reach a final concentration of 1-2 mg/ml.
Combine diluted DNA with phenol red solution to achieve a final concentration of approximately 0.1 mM.
Make a capillary glass microinjection needle using a standard needle puller.
Backfill the glass needle with 5 μl of DNA injection solution using a microloader tip.
Prepare 0.25 g/L Tricaine solution by dissolving Tricaine powder into pre-chilled Holtfreter's solution.
Adjust the pH of the Tricaine solution to be within the range of 6-8 using Tris solution.
Anesthetize the axolotl by placing it in the Tricaine solution for approximately 8 minutes until unresponsive.
Place the axolotl on its belly in an agarose-filled petri dish.
Observe the axolotl under a standard desktop microscope.
Stretch out and position the forelimbs with sterile tweezers to enable injection and subsequent electroporation.
Pressure-inject the DNA injection solution into the axolotl forelimb, approximately 1-2 mm distal to the elbow joint. Use 2-3 different injection sites for full diffusion.
Pour pre-chilled DPBS solution in the petri dish to immerse the injected limb.
Place an electrode tweezer on both sides of the injected forelimb with a distance of 2-4 mm apart between electrodes.

Apply three poring pulses of 150 V and 5 ms with 10 ms interval followed by five transfer pulses of 50 V and 50 ms with 950 ms interval. Hold the proximal part of the forelimb during electroporation using a tweezer.
Amputate the most distal region of the forelimb using a sterile surgical scalpel.
Prepare 0.25 g/L Tricaine solution by dissolving Tricaine powder into pre-chilled Holtfreter's solution.
Adjust the pH of the Tricaine solution to the range of 6-8 using Tris solution.
Anesthetize the axolotl by placing it in the Tricaine solution for approximately 8 minutes until unresponsive to motion.
Cut a sterile hybrislip to 0.8 x 0.8 cm and attach four small particles of adhesive to each corner using sterile tweezers.
Place the anesthetized axolotl inside a sterile fluorodish on its belly, removing major liquid droplets from the dish.
Stretch out the electroporated and amputated forelimb using a sterile tweezer.
Mount the prepared hybrislip onto the blastema region with minimal force applied to each corner of the hybrislip.
Fill the fluorodish with Tricaine solution to submerge the axolotl.
Perform standard confocal imaging on the mounted live axolotl at the site of the blastema using the least possible laser power for imaging.
Perform anesthesia and mounting strictly in the dark for optogenetic experiments.
Use a red flashlight to aid the process during optogenetic experiments.
Use short pulses of 488 nm laser to activate optoATVs.
